subject: Future Tech
title: Aging and Gene Editing
description: A 60-second lesson on Aging and Gene Editing.

hook.text: Aging is driven by accumulating DNA damage, shortening telomeres, and failing cellular repair.

buildup.text: Scientists extended the lifespan of mice by editing genes that control inflammation and cellular senescence.

discovery.text: The Yamanaka factors can reprogram old cells to a younger state. Partial reprogramming in mice reversed signs of aging.

twist.text: Full reprogramming turns cells into stem cells, which can cause tumors. The dose must be precisely controlled.

climax.text: Altos Labs raised $3 billion to pursue cellular rejuvenation. Reversing aging is now a serious, funded research field.

punchline.text: Gene editing may not cure death, but it could postpone it.

quiz.question: What can Yamanaka factors do to old cells?
options: Reprogram them to a younger state
